# The bitopological settling site is a Grothendieck site

The pretopology of pairwise-Stone fiber covers on $\mathbf{T}^*_{\mathrm{site}}$ generates a Grothendieck topology $J$, making $(\mathbf{T}^*, J)$ a [site](../objects/bitopological-settling-site.md).

## Proof

Verify the three Grothendieck axioms ([@maclane-moerdijk1992] Ch. III §2).

**Maximality.** The total sieve at $(q, \tau, U)$ is generated by the singleton $\{\mathrm{id}_{(q, \tau, U)}\}$, which is a covering family with $U_1 = U$. Hence $J(q, \tau, U)$ contains the total sieve. ✓

**Stability under pullback.** Let $\{(q, \tau, U_i) \to (q, \tau, U)\}$ be a covering family and $g : (q', \tau', U') \to (q, \tau, U)$ any morphism. The pullback $U_i \times_U U'$ exists in $\mathbf{T}^*_{\mathrm{site}}$ as $(q', \tau', U' \cap (f \times h)^*(U_i))$, and the family

$$\{(q', \tau', U' \cap (f \times h)^*(U_i)) \to (q', \tau', U')\}_i$$

is a covering family because $(f \times h)^*$ — the composite dualized [predicate](teaching/explanations/predicate.md)-generator and dualized settling advancement — preserves the pairwise-Stone structure (per-generator dualization in the [dualized closure 2-comonad](../morphisms/dualized-closure-2-comonad.md), and standard Priestley-topology preservation under $\mathrm{Cl}^*$), and pairwise-Stone cover-preimages remain pairwise-Stone covers. ✓

**Transitivity.** Given $S \in J(q, \tau, U)$ and a sieve $T$ at $(q, \tau, U)$ such that $T$'s pullback along every morphism in $S$ lies in $J$ at the target: $S$ is generated by pairwise-Stone clopens $\{U_i\}$ with $\bigcup_i U_i = U$; each $T$-pullback is generated by $\{U_{i, j}\}_j$ with $\bigcup_j U_{i, j} = U_i$. So $\bigcup_{i, j} U_{i, j} = \bigcup_i U_i = U$, making $\{U_{i, j}\}$ a pairwise-Stone cover of $U$ that generates a covering sieve contained in $T$. Hence $T \in J$. ✓ $\square$

## Remark — basis status

The pretopology is closed under pullback (preimages of pairwise-Stone covers under Priestley morphisms are pairwise-Stone covers), so it is a Grothendieck *basis*. The associated topology is directly derivable, simplifying site-morphism arguments.
